title: Uganda begins emergency food handouts after 19 die from hunger
description:
Government move follows months of drought and crop failures in Karamoja, with 1.5m people facing malnutrition

Uganda has launched emergency food relief distribution after at least 19 deaths from hunger were reported in an area of prolonged drought in the east of the country.

A crisis has been building in the Karamoja region of Uganda as crops have failed without the season’s expected rains, leaving the region’s 1.5 million people facing acute food shortages and rising malnutrition.

Continue reading...
summary: Uganda has launched emergency food relief distribution in the Karamoja region after 19 deaths from hunger were reported due to prolonged drought and crop failures, affecting 1.5 million people. The region has been experiencing acute food shortages and rising malnutrition. The government's move aims to provide aid to those in need.

title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying
description:
The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year

Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.

Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin were sentenced to eight and 11 years in jail respectively. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities.

Continue reading...
summary: Two Russian men, Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin, have been convicted by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying, and sentenced to 8 and 11 years in jail respectively, for allegedly planning a coup and organizing deadly demonstrations in Angola last year. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in the country for cultural and business activities.

title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers
description:
September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences

The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.

While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.

Continue reading...
summary: The British army has canceled its training exercise in Kenya due to a dispute over a bilateral defence agreement. The Kenyan government refused to ratify the agreement, seeking changes to give local authorities more power to prosecute British soldiers. This move has resulted in the cancellation of the September training exercise.

title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.

The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.

summary: A UK resident who worked in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is being monitored for Ebola at a London hospital after potential exposure to the virus. The individual was medically evacuated from the DRC, where they were treating patients with the disease. The UK Health Security Agency is overseeing the situation.

title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds
description:
Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well

One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.

There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.

Continue reading...
summary: A new UN report finds that one in three people globally cannot afford a healthy diet, with 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs. This highlights the need for urgent action on food affordability to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030. Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025, but experts warn that more work is needed.
